nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
Two separate forward passes through a DistributedDataParallel-wrapped module containing BatchNorm before a single backward() raises:
RuntimeError: one of the variables needed for gradient computation has been modified
by an inplace operation: [torch.cuda.FloatTensor [768]] is at version 3; expected version 2
instead.

This is the standard GAN discriminator training pattern (forward on fake, forward on real; one combined backward). It works correctly without DDP.
Root Cause
DDP's _pre_forward() calls _sync_buffers() before every forward pass when broadcast_buffers=True (default). This runs dist._broadcast_coalesced() on all module buffers, which performs an in-place copy_() on running_mean and running_var of every BatchNorm layer. EDIT: I traced the error below but won't dump the entire thesis here.
Minimal reproducer
"""
Run with: torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=2 repro.py
"""
import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.nn.parallel import DistributedDataParallel as DDP

def main():
    dist.init_process_group(backend="nccl")
    rank = dist.get_rank()
    torch.cuda.set_device(rank)

    disc = nn.Sequential(
        nn.Conv2d(3, 64, 4, 2, 1),
        nn.BatchNorm2d(64),
        nn.LeakyReLU(0.2),
        nn.Conv2d(64, 1, 4, 2, 1),
    ).cuda()

    disc_ddp = DDP(disc, device_ids=[rank])  # broadcast_buffers=True by default
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(disc_ddp.parameters(), lr=1e-4)

    fake = torch.randn(2, 3, 32, 32, device="cuda")
    real = torch.randn(2, 3, 32, 32, device="cuda")

    opt.zero_grad()
    with torch.amp.autocast("cuda"):
        logits_fake = disc_ddp(fake.detach())  # 1st forward: BN + buffer sync
        logits_real = disc_ddp(real.detach())  # 2nd forward: buffer sync bumps version

    loss = -logits_real.mean() + logits_fake.mean()
    loss.backward()  # RuntimeError!
    opt.step()

    print(f"Rank {rank}: OK")
    dist.destroy_process_group()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
Without DDP doesn't raise an error. Something else to mention is I tried a workaround with torch.no_grad(), but this didn't suppress the version counter bump.
Workarounds

Setting broadcast_buffers=False in the DDP constructor eliminates the error, though this disables BatchNorm stat syncs:

disc_ddp = DDP(disc, device_ids=[rank], broadcast_buffers=False)

Concatenated forward - single forward = single buffer sync, though this essentially halves the maximum possible batch size:

combined = torch.cat([fake.detach(), real.detach()], dim=0)
logits = disc_ddp(combined)
logits_fake, logits_real = logits.chunk(2, dim=0)

SyncBatchNorm may avoid the issue since it has its own syncing, but I haven't attempted this workaround to say for sure.

Suggested Improvements

Skip version bumps for buffer sync - the broadcast buffer's copy_() should use torch.autograd._unsafe_preserve_version_counter to avoid unnecessary version bumps on buffers that don't even participate in gradient computation.
Improve error message: When the bumped tensor is a registered buffer (no requires_grad), the error message should mention that DDP buffer sync may be the cause and suggest broadcast_buffers=False as a diagnostic. torch.autograd.set_detect_anomaly(True) isn't much help here either:

Hint: the backtrace further above shows the operation that failed to compute its gradient. 
The variable in question was changed in there or anywhere later. Good luck!


Documentation: Add a note to the DDP docs warning about multiple forward passes through BatchNorm-containing modules, and recommend the concatenated-forward pattern for GAN training.

CUDA 12.4, NCCL 2.21
Tested on NVIDIA H200 and A100

nodes.bodyText:
User MemPool and CUDA graph capture both rely on the same internal state (captures_underway in CUDACachingAllocator) to manage memory pool routing. However, the allocator currently checks captures_underway.empty() to trigger graph capture-specific logic, unintentionally applying these behaviors to both graph capture and user mempool usage.
As a result, when user mempools are active, two major bugs arise:

the deferral of block freeing, intended only for graph capture, is incorrectly used in user mempools
OOM recovery mechanisms are disabled during user mempool contexts.

I reported this problem months ago; see #168137 for details.
Bug 1: Block-free deferral mechanism incorrectly applied to user pools
In free(), when a block has been used on multiple streams:
// c10/cuda/CUDACachingAllocator.cpp, free()
if (!block->stream_uses.empty()) {
    if (C10_UNLIKELY(!captures_underway.empty())) {
        // Defer the free -- meant for graph capture only
        deferred_blocks.emplace(block, ...);
    } else {
        insert_events(block);  // normal path
    }
}
And in malloc(), process_events() is skipped:
// c10/cuda/CUDACachingAllocator.cpp, malloc()
if (C10_LIKELY(captures_underway.empty())) {
    process_events(context);  // queries cudaEvents to recycle blocks
} else {
    // graph_capture_record_stream_reuse path (if enabled)
    free_safe_blocks_in_capture(context, stream);
}
Since use_mem_pool pushes onto captures_underway, the user-pool path hits the graph-capture branch. Blocks with multi-stream usage are put into deferred_blocks instead of having events inserted. And process_events is skipped, so even single-stream event-based blocks are not recycled. The free_safe_blocks_in_capture path is a no-op for user pools because cudaStreamGetCaptureInfo returns cudaStreamCaptureStatusNone.
Impact: Under a user mempool, any block that has been recordStream'd to a second stream becomes unreclaimable for the entire duration of the use_mem_pool context. The memory is held in deferred_blocks or the event queue with no mechanism to process it, increasing memory pressure.
Bug 2: OOM recovery blocked under user pools
The allocator's last-resort retry in malloc():
// c10/cuda/CUDACachingAllocator.cpp, malloc()
block_found = alloc_block(params, false, context, lock)
    || try_mempool_fallback(...)
    || (release_available_cached_blocks(params, context) &&
        alloc_block(params, false, context, lock))
    // Last resort: free ALL cached blocks and retry
    || (C10_LIKELY(captures_underway.empty()) &&
        release_cached_blocks(context, {0, 0}) &&
        alloc_block(params, true, context, lock));
The final fallback is gated on captures_underway.empty(). During graph capture this is correct, since release_cached_blocks calls cudaEventSynchronize, which are illegal during capture. But for user mempools, no capture is happening, and these APIs are perfectly safe.
Impact: When a user mempool accumulates cached blocks (from prior allocations that were freed back to the caching allocator) and a new allocation request exceeds the largest individual cached block, the allocator cannot reclaim its own cached memory. It fails with OOM even though the device has plenty of reclaimable memory.
This is the root cause of a real-world issue in SGLang reported by @nvcastet here sgl-project/sglang#17089.
Reproducer
I asked Claude to generate this reproducer. Both tests FAIL on current PyTorch:

test_mempool_bugs.py (click to expand)
import sys
import torch

PASS = 0
FAIL = 0

def report(name, passed, detail=""):
    global PASS, FAIL
    if passed:
        PASS += 1
    else:
        FAIL += 1
    print(f"[{'PASS' if passed else 'FAIL'}] {name}")
    if detail:
        print(f"       {detail}")


def test_defer_mechanism():
    """Bug 1: multi-stream block frees are deferred under user mempool.

    During graph capture, the allocator defers multi-stream block frees
    because events cannot be meaningfully queried (kernels are recorded,
    not executed). For user pools, kernels execute normally, so the block
    should be recyclable after synchronization."""
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    pool = torch.cuda.MemPool()
    s2 = torch.cuda.Stream()

    with torch.cuda.use_mem_pool(pool):
        a = torch.empty(1024 * 1024, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
        ptr = a.data_ptr()

        with torch.cuda.stream(s2):
            a.record_stream(s2)
            _ = a + 1

        del a
        torch.cuda.synchronize()

        b = torch.empty(1024 * 1024, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
        reused = b.data_ptr() == ptr
        del b

    report(
        "Block free not deferred under user mempool",
        reused,
        "Block was NOT recycled after sync. The free was deferred into "
        "deferred_blocks and process_events was skipped, as if under "
        "graph capture." if not reused else "",
    )
    
def test_oom_recovery():
    """Bug 2: OOM recovery skipped under user mempool.

    Mirrors the real-world reproducer: allocate in a doubling pattern
    (1 GiB, 2 GiB, 4 GiB, ...) so each freed allocation caches a block
    too small for the next request, forcing a fresh cudaMalloc each time.
    Eventually the GPU runs out of fresh memory.  The default allocator
    recovers via release_cached_blocks (frees ALL cached blocks and
    retries).  Under use_mem_pool this path is gated on
    captures_underway.empty() and is skipped, so the allocation fails
    even though the device has plenty of reclaimable cached memory."""
    device = torch.device("cuda:0")
    pool = torch.cuda.MemPool()
    gib = 1024 ** 3

    def max_doubling_alloc(use_pool):
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
        max_size = 0
        size = 1
        try:
            while size < 2000:
                if use_pool:
                    with torch.cuda.use_mem_pool(pool):
                        torch.empty(gib * size, dtype=torch.uint8, device=device)
                else:
                    torch.empty(gib * size, dtype=torch.uint8, device=device)
                max_size = size
                size *= 2
        except Exception:
            pass
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
        return max_size

    max_default = max_doubling_alloc(use_pool=False)
    max_pool = max_doubling_alloc(use_pool=True)

    report(
        "OOM recovery works under user mempool",
        max_pool >= max_default,
        f"Default allocator max: {max_default} GiB, "
        f"MemPool max: {max_pool} GiB. "
        f"MemPool hit OOM because release_cached_blocks was skipped "
        f"(gated on captures_underway.empty())."
        if max_pool < max_default else "",
    )



def main():
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        print("CUDA not available.")
        sys.exit(1)
    print(f"PyTorch {torch.__version__}")
    print(f"CUDA device: {torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)}\n")
    test_defer_mechanism()
    test_oom_recovery()
    print(f"\nResults: {PASS} passed, {FAIL} failed")
    sys.exit(1 if FAIL else 0)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Proposed Fix
Rather than that full refactoring in #168137, We can targeted minimal fix as what @ngimel suggested, keeping the existing structures and handling operations differently depending on configuration.
Add a bool is_graph_capture flag to each entry in the captures_underway vector (via beginAllocateToPool). CUDAGraph::capture_begin would pass is_graph_capture=true; use_mem_pool would pass false. A new predicate graph_capture_underway() would return true only when any entry has the flag set. The safety guards (deferring frees, skipping process_events, blocking release_cached_blocks) would switch from captures_underway.empty() to graph_capture_underway(), so they only activate during actual graph capture. Pool routing continues to use captures_underway as before, both graph capture and user pools still need it.
Separately, @galv raised the idea of directly querying cudaStreamIsCapturing() at allocation/free time to distinguish capture state, rather than relying on internal bookkeeping. That could be another alternative.
